correctness.rationale: An eight-state column generator defines an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain. Stationary Poisson corrector differentiation gives exact mean and Fano rational functions. The standalone verifier reconstructs every coefficient of these functions and derivative polynomials; all derivative denominators have positive coefficients. Descartes variations 0,1,1,2 and exact rational intermediate sign evaluations give respectively 0,1,1,2 positive simple critical points, whose sign types and endpoints are stated. Independent 24-dimensional count-moment ODE computations pass at 20 channel/parameter combinations. Finite tests check implementation; full quantifiers follow from exact algebra and sign proofs.

originality.rationale: The precise all-positive-rate four-channel Fano response classification and the two simple desorption extrema are not stated or entailed by the inspected 2026 TASEP-LK density/correlation results, by the published defect-ring current fluctuation study, or by the accessible same-chain equal-adsorption/equal-desorption counting classification. The latter varies a different path through the two-rate parameter plane, and the present one-parameter extrema are not restrictions of it. Search is not an exhaustive priority proof.

A generic full-counting-statistics treatment could cover this exact finite-state specialization without naming the specific rates.

value.rationale: The three-site chain is the smallest open TASEP–Langmuir system with a genuine interior adsorption/desorption site and both transport bonds. Holding desorption and all contact rates fixed while scanning adsorption is an experimentally/kinetically coherent control direction. Distinct count channels respond by 0,1,1,2 critical points, including a nontrivial desorption reentrance that stationary occupancy or mean-current information cannot predict. The complete exact classification provides a strict benchmark for finite-chain counting statistics; the small desorption excursion and lack of finite-window claims are acknowledged.
